issue.title: [notifications-v1 04/05] Deliver notifications through Web Push and APNs (#151)

body:
Relay BB run pushed an update.

Pull request: #362

Tokens: 0 · Cost: $0.0000

Branch `bb/relay-151-notifications-v1-04-05-deliver-notific-thr_c986iktz3g` pushed to origin successfully.

## Summary

Implements issue #151: delivering committed notifications through Web Push and APNs.

- **`writeNotification`** now enqueues one `notificationFanout` graphile-worker job per genuinely-new notification (dedup via `RETURNING id` on the existing `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` insert), keyed by the notification's own id so the job can never be duplicated even if the caller replays.
- **`notificationFanout` job handler** loads every active `push_subscriptions` registration for the notification's user and dispatches each through its channel's adapter — Web Push (VAPID, via the `web-push` package) or APNs (raw HTTP/2, ES256 provider JWT cached for up to 55 minutes, sandbox/production host selected from `apns_environment`).
- **`push_deliveries`** (new migration 0032) is the durable per-(notification, registration) dedup key: a unique index on `(notification_id, push_subscription_id)` plus a three-state status (pending/delivered/permanently-failed) guarantees a retried job run never re-sends a pair that already succeeded or was already ruled out.
- Transient provider/network failures leave the delivery row pending and rethrow so graphile-worker retries the whole job; a permanent rejection (404/410/`BadDeviceToken`) marks that one delivery failed and invalidates only that registration via #150's `revokePushSubscriptionByProviderInvalidation`.
- Notification payloads sent to providers are limited to `notification_id`, `title`, and `link_href` — no source content beyond the notification row.

## Verification

- TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and `dependency-cruiser` boundary checks: all clean
- Unit tests: 127/127 passed
- Integration tests: 857/857 passed (74 files), including 8 new tests covering exactly-once fanout, revoked-registration skipping, cross-retry idempotency, partial transient-failure retry, and permanent-failure scoped revocation
- E2E tests: 5/5 passed

- **`writeNotification`** enqueues one `notificationFanout` graphile-worker job per genuinely-new notification, keyed by the notification's own id.

## Review fixes (this update)

Addressed all three findings from the automated code review on PR #362, in `apnsAdapter.ts`:
- **High:** `aps.alert.body` was set to the same string as `title`, duplicating the title as body on every iOS notification. `notifications` has no separate body/description column, so the alert now carries `title` only.
- **Medium:** `postApnsRequest` had no timeout — an unresponsive APNs host could hang the promise indefinitely, blocking a graphile-worker task slot. Added a 10s timeout that fails the request and tears down the HTTP/2 client.
- **Medium:** the HTTP/2 client-level error handler rejected without closing the session, leaking the socket on TLS/session-level failures. It now goes through the same cleanup path as every other failure, always calling `client.destroy()`.

- Integration tests: 857/857 passed (74 files), including 8 tests covering exactly-once fanout, revoked-registration skipping, cross-retry idempotency, partial transient-failure retry, and permanent-failure scoped revocation

## Summary

Implements issue #151: delivering committed notifications through Web Push and APNs.

- Payloads to providers are limited to `notification_id`, `title`, and `link_href`.

## Review fixes (this update)

Addressed all four findings from the latest automated code review round on PR #362:
- **High:** `getNotificationById` and `getPushDeliveryStatuses` called `client.query()` without a generic type parameter, so `rows` was `any[]` and the hand-written row shapes on the consuming code performed no actual check. Both now use `client.query<RowShape>(...)`.
- **High:** the APNs response `reason` field was read via an unchecked `as` cast on parsed JSON from an external API; a non-string value would have silently defeated the `BadDeviceToken` comparison and retried a permanently-dead device token forever. Extracted into `extractReason()`, which validates the shape before returning it.
- **Medium:** the APNs response body accumulator had no size bound. Added a 64 KiB ceiling that fails the request if exceeded.

(A prior review round's three findings — duplicated alert body, missing request timeout, and a socket leak on HTTP/2 client-level errors, all in `apnsAdapter.ts` — were already fixed and confirmed by CI as resolved.)
